item.title: [Recap] Grayson Allen (CHA): Grayson Allen provided a boost off the bench with 20 points (6-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday.
item.description:
Grayson Allen provided a boost off the bench with 20 points (6-of-12 FGs), three rebounds, five assists, one steal and four three-pointers against the Heat on Saturday.

Allen hasn’t started in place of Kon Knueppel (hamstring), but he has been able to fill the shooting void. That included a clutch four-point play in this game, which gave the Hornets a lead that they didn’t relinquish. Allen is rostered in just 33 percent of Yahoo! leagues, but with how many threes Charlotte shoots as a team, Allen should be rostered until Knueppel returns.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Dennis Schröder (CHA): Dennis Schröder lit up the Heat with 25 points (8-of-17 FGs), six rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers on Saturday.
item.description:
Dennis Schröder lit up the Heat with 25 points (8-of-17 FGs), six rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers on Saturday.

After struggling in Friday’s blowout loss to the Hawks, Schröder was able to bounce back with his best performance of the season. Two of his three starts in place of Coby White (calf) have been productive, with the one poor performance coming in a 47-point loss that was bad for the entire team. Schröder is worth streaming until White returns to the lineup. He’s currently rostered in just 26 percent of Yahoo! leagues.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Brandon Miller (CHA): Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 34 points (10-of-29 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers in a 115-110 win over the Heat on Saturday.
item.description:
Brandon Miller led the Hornets with 34 points (10-of-29 FGs, 11-of-12 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers in a 115-110 win over the Heat on Saturday.

Miller has been the focal point of the offense for Charlotte early on this year, which gives him a green light to shoot often. He is averaging 21.3 shot attempts per game this season, and while he still isn’t shooting efficiently, he was able to pour in the points in this one. The difference in this game was the free throw rate. He shot three total free throws in their first two games, far less than his 12 attempts in this one. Miller is going to continue to get as many shots as he wants until Kon Knueppel (hamstring) returns. He should be in for more big scoring nights, especially when his shot starts falling at a higher rate.

Noah Rubin

item.title: DeAndre Jordan (NOP): Jeremiah Fears, Dejounte Murray, Trey Murphy, Zion Williamson and DeAndre Jordan will start Saturday’s game against the Nuggets.
item.description:
Jeremiah Fears, Dejounte Murray, Trey Murphy, Zion Williamson and DeAndre Jordan will start Saturday’s game against the Nuggets.

With Yves Missi suffering a bone bruise in his knee during Friday’s loss to the Jazz, the Pelicans had a hole to fill at center. Instead of Derik Queen, Jordan will fill the void. While an interesting choice, Jordan offers better defense than Queen.

item.title: [Recap] Naz Reid (CHA): Naz Reid lit up the Heat with 23 points (9-of-16 FGs), nine rebounds, two blocks and five three-pointers on Saturday.
item.description:
Naz Reid lit up the Heat with 23 points (9-of-16 FGs), nine rebounds, two blocks and five three-pointers on Saturday.

Reid has been productive in his first season as a Hornet, but this was his highest-scoring performance so far this year. It was also his best field goal percentage and the most triples he’s knocked down in a game this season. Reid has fit in flawlessly with Charlotte’s three-point heavy approach on offense, and he should continue to have some strong scoring nights. Any extra value he can add in other categories will just be a cherry on top.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Davion Mitchell (MIA): Davion Mitchell led the Heat with 22 points (8-of-13 FGs), one rebound, 10 assists, one steal and three three-pointers in a 15-110 loss to the Hornets on Saturday.
item.description:
Davion Mitchell led the Heat with 22 points (8-of-13 FGs), one rebound, 10 assists, one steal and three three-pointers in a 15-110 loss to the Hornets on Saturday.

Miami trailed by 21 points entering the fourth quarter, but Mitchell fueled a monster comeback, mostly with Giannis Antetokounmpo on the bench. That didn’t result in a win, but it was another strong performance for him. He has been fantastic this year, averaging 17.0 points, 8.7 assists and 2.3 three-pointers per game, all of which would be career bests for him. He has been a bright spot despite a rough start to the year for Miami.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Bam Adebayo (MIA): Bam Adebayo finished with 20 points (7-of-17 FGs), eight rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers on Saturday against the Hornets.
item.description:
Bam Adebayo finished with 20 points (7-of-17 FGs), eight rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers on Saturday against the Hornets.

It has been a rough start to the year for Bam, but after totaling 19 points in Miami’s first two games, he was able to surpass that mark in this one. It wasn’t enough for them to get in the win column, but it was good to see him have a productive outing. He’ll try to build on this performance in their next game, which comes against the Mavericks on Monday.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Giannis Antetokounmpo (MIA): Giannis Antetokounmpo finished with 14 points (4-of-11 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, three assists and one steal against the Hornets on Saturday.
item.description:
Giannis Antetokounmpo finished with 14 points (4-of-11 FGs, 6-of-8 FTs), six rebounds, three assists and one steal against the Hornets on Saturday.

So far this season, the story for Miami has been that Giannis hasn’t had enough help. Well, his teammates stepped up more in this game, but Antetokounmpo wasn’t quite as productive. They went on a big run without him to tie things up in the fourth quarter. He entered with about four minutes left, committed two fouls in three minutes, and the Hornets took a six-point lead. It was a rough performance for him, but there is no reason for managers to worry. He averaged 35.5 points through their first two games and should get back on track against the Mavericks on Monday.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Injury] Paolo Banchero (ORL): ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Paolo Banchero suffered a low-grade high ankle sprain and could miss 4-to-6 weeks.
item.description:
ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Paolo Banchero suffered a low-grade high ankle sprain and could miss 4-to-6 weeks.

Banchero tweaked his right ankle early in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves. The 23-year-old forward returned after going to the locker room, but the team shut him down midway through the fourth quarter. A high ankle sprain could sideline Banchero for 4-to-6 weeks, which is potentially devastating news for the 0-2 Magic. Orlando will the face the Knicks on Sunday and at this point it’s unlikely Banchero suits up with Tristan da Silva being the most likely to replace him in the starting lineup.

item.title: [Recap] Yaxel Lendeborg (GSW): Yaxel Lendeborg notched 18 points (4-of-11 FGs, 9-of-12 FTs), 13 rebounds, six assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies.
item.description:
Yaxel Lendeborg notched 18 points (4-of-11 FGs, 9-of-12 FTs), 13 rebounds, six assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies.

After a much-discussed debut in the Warriors’ loss to the Lakers on Wednesday, Lendeborg recorded his first career double-double on Friday. The rookie’s final stat line lacked only a blocked shot, but he has all the makings of a player who will offer consistent value in fantasy basketball. Stephen Curry (ankle) is not expected to play in Saturday’s game against the Suns, and Brandin Podziemski (back) has already been ruled out. If Lendeborg is sitting on your league’s waiver wire, don’t hesitate to pick him up.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Brandin Podziemski (GSW): Brandin Podziemski (head) accounted for 18 points (7-of-17 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, three steals, one block and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies.
item.description:
Brandin Podziemski (head) accounted for 18 points (7-of-17 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, three assists, three steals, one block and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies.

Podziemski entered Friday’s game dealing with a sore lower back that kept him out of Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers. It didn’t help matters that he took an inadvertent forearm from Grizzlies center Zach Edey to the head early in the first quarter. Podziemski returned later in the period after a trip to the locker room and logged 33 minutes overall. He finished with a complete stat line, but this is it for Podz in Week 1. After Friday’s defeat, he said he would not play in Saturday’s game against the Suns.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Graham Ike (GSW): Graham Ike produced 10 points (4-of-7 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies.
item.description:
Graham Ike produced 10 points (4-of-7 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies.

After starting Draymond Green at center in Wednesday’s loss to the Lakers, Warriors head coach Steve Kerr opted against that approach on Friday. As a result, Ike made his first NBA start. The rookie from Gonzaga shot reasonably well, but he offered little value beyond points and three-pointers. The Warriors visit Phoenix on Saturday, and Ike may play more, as Al Horford hasn’t played both games of back-to-backs in a few years.

Raphielle Johnson

Stephen Curry tallied 24 points (5-of-15 FGs, 11-of-11 FTs), three rebounds, four assists and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Grizzlies.

Curry led the Warriors in scoring on Friday, but he shot a frigid 5-of-15 from the field. The assists were solid, but this was not the best night to have the Warriors star in most fantasy lineups. After the game, Curry said he “probably” won’t play against the Suns on Saturday, bad news for fantasy managers hoping for a bounce-back effort.

item.title: [Recap] Gregory Jackson (MEM): GG Jackson finished Friday’s win over the Warriors with two points (1-of-6 FGs), four rebounds and one assist.
item.description:
GG Jackson finished Friday’s win over the Warriors with two points (1-of-6 FGs), four rebounds and one assist.

With Cedric Coward (wrist) unavailable, Jackson moved into the starting lineup on Friday. Unfortunately for those who streamed him, GG offered little value as a spot starter. He picked up four fouls in 10 first-half minutes, and Kris Murray (three rebounds, one assist, and one block) would start the third quarter. Whether or not Jackson gets another opportunity on Sunday against the Kings depends on Coward’s health, but he may not be worth the streaming risk in most leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Isaiah Stewart (MEM): Isaiah Stewart notched four points (2-of-3 FGs), two rebounds and one steal in Friday’s win over the Warriors.
item.description:
Isaiah Stewart notched four points (2-of-3 FGs), two rebounds and one steal in Friday’s win over the Warriors.

Stewart made his official Grizzlies debut on Friday, playing most of his minutes when starting center Zach Edey (8/10/3/1/2) was not on the floor. Unfortunately, Beef Stew picked up four fouls in the first half, including three in the first quarter, which limited him to 16 minutes. It remains to be seen what his role will look like once the ankle is no longer a concern, but Stewart isn’t someone worth rostering in most redraft leagues just yet.

After recording 12 points and four steals in Wednesday’s season-opening win over the Jazz, Wells was more productive offensively against the Warriors. He scored an efficient 17 points, a number he met or exceeded in 18 of 69 appearances last season. Wells still isn’t at the point where he’s a must-roster player, but he should have more room to produce, especially on nights when Cedric Coward (wrist) doesn’t play.

item.title: [Recap] Ty Jerome (MEM): Ty Jerome accounted for 28 points (11-of-22 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Warriors.
item.description:
Ty Jerome accounted for 28 points (11-of-22 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, five assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Warriors.

After scoring 45 points in Wednesday’s opener, Jerome appeared to be coming down to earth in the first half of Friday’s game. However, after scoring eight first-half points on 3-of-7 shooting, the Grizzlies point guard put up 14 points in the third quarter. Jerome and the Grizzlies ripped off a 17-0 run in the fourth to move to 2-0 on the season, getting their four-game road trip off to a good start.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Cameron Boozer (MEM): Cameron Boozer finished Friday’s win over the Warriors with 25 points (6-of-13 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), 13 rebounds, six assists, two steals and four three-pointers.
item.description:
Cameron Boozer finished Friday’s win over the Warriors with 25 points (6-of-13 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), 13 rebounds, six assists, two steals and four three-pointers.

After struggling with his shot in his NBA debut on Wednesday, Boozer had a much better night against the Warriors. The rookie forward made four of his first five three-point attempts and scored 14 points in the first half. By the end of the night, Boozer had made franchise history, becoming the second-youngest Grizzly to record a double-double. Memphis ends its Week 1 with a game against the Kings on Sunday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Darius Garland (LAC): Darius Garland finished Friday’s loss to the Lakers with 26 points (9-of-19 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six assists, one steal and four three-pointers.
item.description:
Darius Garland finished Friday’s loss to the Lakers with 26 points (9-of-19 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six assists, one steal and four three-pointers.

The star guards in this matchup all seemed to struggle with turnovers. Garland racked up nine, while the Lakers’ Luka Dončić (11) and Austin Reaves (six) combined for 17. Garland had a solid night shooting the basketball, but nine-cat managers took a hit because of the turnovers. He’ll look to finish Week 1 on a high note when the Clippers visit the Thunder on Sunday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Brook Lopez (LAC): Brook Lopez tallied 22 points (8-of-9 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, three blocks and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Brook Lopez tallied 22 points (8-of-9 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, three blocks and two three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Lakers.

While Isaiah Jackson (six points, six rebounds, three assists, three steals, and one block in 28 minutes) earned the starting center role, his limited offensive skill set means Clippers head coach Tyronn Lue will continue to factor Lopez into his plans. Against the Lakers, the 7-foot-1 backup scored 15 points on 6-of-6 shooting in the first half on Friday. Lopez’s production tailed off after halftime, but his final line reminded everyone what he can do, even in a backup role.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Donovan Clingan (POR): Donovan Clingan scored 8 points (3-of-5 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), ten rebounds, three assists, and two blocks in 19 minutes against the Kings.
item.description:
Donovan Clingan scored 8 points (3-of-5 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), ten rebounds, three assists, and two blocks in 19 minutes against the Kings.

Clingan had some foul trouble in this game and the Blazers went small which resulted in lower minutes for Clingan. He still produced when he was out there, but it was obviously not what you were hoping for. This happened last year at times and there will be more games this year where its in the best of the Blazers to have him on the bench. He’ll have his next opportunity against the Lakers where he will need to play more minutes against Walker Kessler.

item.title: [Recap] Rui Hachimura (LAC): Rui Hachimura recorded 16 points (5-of-14 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Rui Hachimura recorded 16 points (5-of-14 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, two steals and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Lakers.

Playing against his former team for the first time since signing with the Clippers in free agency, Hachimura struggled with his shot. He’s started slowly, shooting 8-of-27 from the field in the Clippers’ first two games. Given the team’s lack of reliable scorers, the shot volume will be there. However, it won’t mean much if Hachimura can’t hit shots at a higher clip. He’s a career 49.8 percent shooter, which suggests that Rui will turn things around. But things won’t get any easier, as the Clippers visit the Thunder on Sunday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Damian Lillard (POR): Damian Lillard with 19 points (7-of-18 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, two steals, a block and two 3-pointers in Blazers win over the Kings.
item.description:
Damian Lillard with 19 points (7-of-18 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, two steals, a block and two 3-pointers in Blazers win over the Kings.

It wasn’t the most efficient night for Damian Lillard, but he still gave you a good game. As he’s coming back from his Achilles injury, he will have some nights where he is not very efficient, especially early on the season. We weren’t drafting Damian Lillard as high as we have been, so there isn’t much to complain about when there’s the occasional inefficient night.

item.title: [Recap] Matisse Thybulle (LAL): Matisse Thybulle accounted for 13 points (5-of-8 FGs), one rebound, two assists, two steals, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Clippers.
item.description:
Matisse Thybulle accounted for 13 points (5-of-8 FGs), one rebound, two assists, two steals, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Clippers.

Could Thybulle return to relevance in fantasy basketball with the Lakers? His defense earned the veteran wing a starting spot, and he played well on both ends of the floor in Friday’s win. In addition to his three defensive contributions, Thybulle shot 3-of-6 from beyond the arc. He’s a career 34.9 percent shooter from deep, so managers shouldn’t expect high-level production there. However, the starting role makes Thybulle someone to watch, especially in deep leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Kyshawn George (WAS): Kyshawn George had 11 points (2-of-9 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals, and a three against Raptors.
item.description:
Kyshawn George had 11 points (2-of-9 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, three assists, two steals, and a three against Raptors.

He did get to the line seven times and got you two steals which provided some value because he didn’t hit many shots and gave you unwanted turnovers. The Raptors physicality clearly bothered George in this game as he had 8 turnovers in this game. Until AJ comes back, he’s still worth rostering in redraft leagues.

item.title: [Recap] Wendell Carter (ORL): Wendell Carter Jr. amassed 20 points (8-of-9 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), nine rebounds, one assist, two blocks and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
item.description:
Wendell Carter Jr. amassed 20 points (8-of-9 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), nine rebounds, one assist, two blocks and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Timberwolves.

The offseason signing of Nikola Vučević hasn’t hurt Carter’s playing time, as Vooch has been third in Orlando’s center pecking order in the first two games. After logging 31 minutes in Wednesday’s loss to the Hawks, Carter played 29 minutes against the Timberwolves and led the Magic in points, rebounds, blocks, and three-pointers. He’s never been a great fantasy option, especially in category leagues, but Carter’s start to the season has been encouraging.

item.description:
Leonard Miller had 19 points (7-of-11 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, one block and two three-pointers against the Bucks on Friday.

Miller only played 23 minutes off the bench in this one as Caleb Wilson and Norman Powell were the only Bulls to play at least 30 minutes. Still, it’s impossible to ignore Miller’s production after an impressive preseason and the first two games of the regular season. He’s scored in double figures in both games despite minutes totals in the low-20s. Miller probably needs more minutes to be fantasy-relevant, but at some point he could force his way into a more prominent role in the rotation.

item.title: [Recap] Caleb Wilson (CHI): Caleb Wilson had 21 points (7-of-14 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers against the Bucks on Friday.
item.description:
Caleb Wilson had 21 points (7-of-14 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, one assist, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers against the Bucks on Friday.

After Wilson’s inauspicious debut Wednesday that included 33.3 percent shooting from the field and nine turnovers, the 20-year-old forward bounced back nicely in the second game of his NBA career. He was 7-of-14 from the field (50 percent), scored 21 points and had just three turnovers. Wilson will have ups and downs in his career and there will certainly be more bumps in the road during his rookie season, but this was undoubtedly a promising performance.

Nick Shlain

item.title: [Recap] Norman Powell (CHI): Norman Powell had 25 points (7-of-20 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in the Bulls’ 132-125 victory over the Hawks on Friday.
item.description:
Norman Powell had 25 points (7-of-20 FGs, 9-of-9 FTs), four rebounds, one assist and two three-pointers in the Bulls’ 132-125 victory over the Hawks on Friday.

Powell was the Bulls’ leading scorer in the victory over the Bucks on Wednesday. While he had 25 points, Powell’s typically excellent shooting from behind the three-point line was noticeably absent. The 33-year-old shooting guard went 2-of-12 from behind the arc and is now 4-of-18 (22.2 percent) from long distance this season. Powell is a career 39.6 percent three-point shooter and should have better shooting games in his future as he’s due for positive regression.
